messages.author: 7bdb2cc7d6e9317e
messages.subject: Multiple Dependent Variables in Model
parts:
Hello,


Thank you for taking the time to assist me with my question; your help is greatly appreciated. I have successfully run SEM models using the lavaan package and all of these models had one dependent variable in each mdoel. However, now I am interested in creating a model that contains two dependent variables together. I am interested in this because two dependent variables I am interested in are highly comorbid, so studying them together makes more conceptual sense. I have tried two separate methods so far, but have been unsuccessful.


Method 1 was:


DV1 + DV2 ~ Factor + Interaction + Age + Sex


Method 2 was combining the two dependent variables into one single variable in the variable definition section of the model:


Combined =~ DV1 + DV2

Combined ~ Factor + Interaction + Age + Sex


Both of these methods produced errors. Can you guide me towards the correct direction so that I am able to combine multiple dependent variables into a single model? Thank you again.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Dependent Variables in Model
parts:
Your second approach implies additional constraints that you probably do not intend.
Your first approach is consistent with your description of the problem. You could equivalently code it as:
DV1 ~ Factor + Interaction + Age + Sex
DV2 ~ Factor + Interaction + Age + Sex
What error message did you receive? The more details you can share, the better.
